sections.h2: Where is Twin Falls, Idaho, and what is the city known for?
sections.html:
Twin Falls is the county seat and largest city of Twin Falls County, on a broad plain at the south rim of the Snake River Canyon in south-central Idaho. It is the largest city within a 100-mile radius in the Magic Valley region and the principal city of a metro area that takes in Twin Falls and Jerome counties.

The canyon forms the city's northern edge and separates it from Jerome County. Shoshone Falls, at 213 feet, is 46 feet higher than Niagara Falls. The Perrine Bridge crosses the canyon just north of town, and Evel Knievel attempted his rocket jump across the canyon here in September 1974.

The city covers about 20 square miles. The Census Bureau counted 51,807 residents in 2020, and the estimate for July 1, 2025 on this page is 56,216.

sections.h2: What is Twin Falls' history, and why is the town laid out the way it is?
sections.html:
Twin Falls was founded in 1904 as a planned community and was incorporated as a village on April 12, 1905. It exists because of irrigation. I. B. Perrine started the Twin Falls Land and Water Company in 1900, and Milner Dam, finished in 1905, made commercial irrigation outside the canyon practical for the first time.

The townsite was designed by the architect Emmanuel Louis Masqueray, and lot sales helped pay for the canals. The city became the seat of the new Twin Falls County in 1907. The same irrigation project produced nearby Kimberly, Buhl, Filer, Hansen and Murtaugh.

For a seller, that history explains a few things you may see in a title report or on an older lot: canal and irrigation easements, water-related records and houses from the early and mid twentieth century. If your property has a ditch, canal or shared water right, tell the buyer early and ask the title company what is recorded.

sections.h2: Who are the major employers in Twin Falls?
sections.html:
Twin Falls has long served the agriculture industry, and food processing is still a core part of the local economy. Beans and sugar beets were early commodities, and other processors joined them later.

The employers named on public sources include:

  • Glanbia Foods, a cheese producer.
  • Chobani, which opened what Wikipedia calls the world's largest yogurt plant in Twin Falls in 2012, adding about 300 jobs.
  • Amalgamated Sugar Company, maker of White Satin sugar.
  • Lamb Weston, with a food-processing plant in west Twin Falls.
  • The College of Southern Idaho.
  • St. Luke's Magic Valley, a 700,000-square-foot hospital that opened in the northwest part of the city in spring 2011.

Employer mix matters to sellers because relocations and job changes are one of the most common reasons people sell quickly. If you have accepted a job elsewhere, or a plant shift change has put you in a bind with a second mortgage payment, a sale on your own timeline can matter more than squeezing out the last dollar.

sections.h2: How do roads and getting around work in Twin Falls?
sections.html:
Twin Falls is the largest city in Idaho that is not directly on the Interstate Highway System. U.S. Route 30 and U.S. Route 93 serve it, and Interstate 84 is reached across the canyon on the Perrine Bridge, with the junction about 5 miles north in Jerome County.

State Highway 74 runs south from downtown Twin Falls toward Hollister and Rogerson and on to Jackpot, Nevada. The city passed 50,000 residents, which triggered a federal requirement for a public transit system, and a transit service now operates inside the city limits.

Buyers who commute to Jerome or along I-84 look at which side of the canyon a house sits on, so mention highway access in any description of your property.

sections.h2: What do Twin Falls County's property tax dates mean for a sale?
sections.html:
Twin Falls County mails tax bills by the fourth Monday in November. The first half is due by December 20 and the second half by June 20 of the next year. The Treasurer mails bills, and the Assessor's Office is the contact for address changes; its number is (208) 735-4870.

  • A 2 percent late charge is added to a first half that is not paid by December 20.
  • Interest then accrues from January 1 at 12 percent a year, which is 1 percent a month.
  • The second half carries a 2 percent late charge after June 20, and interest dates back to January 1.
  • Mail payments go to P.O. Box 88, Twin Falls, ID 83303-0088, and the postmark must be on or before the due date.
  • Online card payments carry a 2.5 percent convenience fee, and an e-check costs $2.00. The county keeps none of it.

The county also tells owners to find out whether their lender pays the tax. If you recently refinanced, review the loan documents or ask your title company or lender. Not receiving a notice does not excuse the tax, according to Idaho Code 63-902(9). For questions about a missing bill or a recent purchase, the county lists 208-736-4008.

At a sale, the title company usually divides the current year's tax between you and the buyer on the closing statement, and any unpaid prior balance comes out of your proceeds. Ask for a payoff figure from the Treasurer before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: What permits and zoning rules affect a Twin Falls house?
sections.html:
The city lets you look up zoning by address on its zoning map, and setbacks depend on the zoning designation under City Code. The Planning and Zoning Department is at (208) 735-7267, and Building Safety is at (208) 735-7238.

One rule that comes up with older properties: a shed or accessory building over 200 square feet needs a Zoning Use Permit and a building permit. If you have built a shop, garage or addition without one, a buyer's lender or inspector may flag it. An as-is sale with a cash buyer avoids that financing hurdle, though you should still tell the buyer what was built.

Before you list, gather the items below:

  • Zoning label and any recorded easements.
  • Permit history for additions, garages and sheds.
  • Latest property tax notice and Treasurer balance.
  • Any lease for a tenant living in the house.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work in Twin Falls?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Twin Falls follows the usual Idaho closing steps without a buyer's mortgage. You describe the house, receive a written offer, and decide. A title company handles the deed, pays off liens and settles tax.

Cash Home Buyers purchases houses as-is. There are no fees, commissions or closing costs to you, and you owe nothing if you decline the offer. We do not quote a price before we know your house.

sections.h2: What do Twin Falls sellers commonly deal with?
sections.html:
• Inherited houses where the heirs live out of state and need to confirm who can sign.
  • Homes with deferred maintenance on the roof, heating or plumbing.
  • Rentals with tenants that the owner no longer wants to manage.
  • Owners behind on a mortgage or on the December and June tax installments.

Each of these has a first step. For an inherited house, collect the death certificate and any court paperwork. For tax trouble, get the exact balance from the Treasurer. For a repair-heavy house, write down what is wrong so any buyer can price it. Our Idaho property tax, homestead and estate tax guides, linked on this page, go deeper. This is general information about Twin Falls and is not legal or tax advice.

faqs.q: When are Twin Falls County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due by December 20 and the second half by June 20 of the following year. Tax bills are issued by the fourth Monday in November.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the December 20 payment in Twin Falls County?
faqs.a: A 2 percent late charge is added to the unpaid first half. Interest at 12 percent a year starts accruing January 1.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a shed in Twin Falls?
faqs.a: An accessory building over 200 square feet requires a Zoning Use Permit and a building permit. Call Planning and Zoning at (208) 735-7267 to confirm for your lot.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Twin Falls house that is not in good shape?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer such as Cash Home Buyers purchases as-is, so you do not need to make repairs first. You can still list it with an agent, but the inspection may lead to repair requests.

faqs.q: Is Twin Falls on an interstate?
faqs.a: No. Twin Falls is the largest city in Idaho not directly on the Interstate Highway System. Interstate 84 is reached across the canyon by the Perrine Bridge, about 5 miles north.

faqs.q: Does Cash Home Buyers charge fees in Twin Falls?
faqs.a: No. There are no fees, commissions or closing costs to you, and you owe nothing if you turn the offer down.
